item.title: Said & Checked, Michigan, 2026-11-15: none false or contradicted, 4 unsettled (John Moolenaar)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsettled

  • John Moolenaar, U.S. Representative from Michigan: “Yes, he has. And also representatives from Nvidia. We are in the process of discussing exact dates.” Unsettled. ABC News reported around Nov. 10 that Jensen Huang and Nvidia had not responded to the committee chairs' request for a closed-door briefing on Nov. 18. That predates the statement, so it neither confirms nor rules out a later agreement; no confirmation or refusal by the committee or the company was found.
  • John Moolenaar, U.S. Representative from Michigan: “she's a Chinese national, set up a company that has been able to access over $12 billion of high-end chips. And there's an investigation as to whether those chips were illegally smuggled into China.” Unsettled. CNBC reports, citing Bloomberg, that the U.S. government is investigating whether the company moved Nvidia chips to China, which fits the second part. The "over $12 billion" figure was not found in any official or company record: the pages read give about $2 billion in purchases and $7.5 billion in related imports.
  • John Moolenaar, U.S. Representative from Michigan: “So, anyone who doesn't comply with the CCP can be imprisoned, they or their family members.” Unsettled. The law, as quoted by Wikipedia, requires cooperation with intelligence work, but commentary cited there says it has no enforcement mechanism. No page read documents a person or a relative imprisoned for refusing to cooperate, and "anyone" is loose wording.

13 statements by 2 officeholders. 9 checked: 5 supported, 4 unsettled · 4 not checkable.
